title: Oplet Curator & Verification Harness for Safe Admin Playbooks
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Problem: on-call engineers frequently need tiny, deterministic admin actions (patch user, rotate secret, scale pool) composed into short runbooks. Current runbook assets are freeform scripts or long prose playbooks and are fragile in production, leading to varying operator outcomes and occasional human errors.

Goal: build an 'oplet' curator — a small curated repository of validated, composable admin playlets (oplets) coupled with a verification harness that ensures idempotency, permission checks, and telemetry-driven dry-runs before scheduling to production. The system should allow engineers and SREs to publish new oplets, auto-validate them in a simulated surgical-sandbox, and promote them through canary dry-run -> staged rollout -> catalog availability.

Scope:
- Oplet manifest format (YAML): inputs, outputs, required permissions, abort conditions, safe-mode fallbacks.
- Verification harness: static lints, simulated execution with synthetic context, and replay tests populated from recent incidents.
- Telemetry gating: check live metric deltas (latency, error counts) in a rehearsal window before promotion.
- Integration with Console: catalog UI, per-oplet SLOs, and cost/latency estimates.
- CI hooks: Github PR checks that run static verification and attach a "verified/oplet" badge.

Out of scope for initial MVP: RBAC authoring UI (will use manifest editing + PR flow), full policy engine integration (we'll plug later), and on-prem air-gapped publish flow (phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Define oplet manifest spec and example set of 8 canonical oplets (rotate-key, compact-logs, scale-worker-pool, evacuate-node, update-flag, snapshot-config, reroute-traffic, revoke-session)
Verification harness runs on PRs and reports pass/fail with logs attached (Github Actions reference)
Simulated surgical-sandbox can replay at least 3 recent incidents with no stateful side-effects and produces deterministic expected outputs
Console shows oplet in catalog with verified badge, SLO, and estimated cost/latency
Staged rollout workflow: dev -> rehearsal -> canary-dryrun -> promoted (manual approval step)
design_decisions: Manifests will be YAML with a strict schema; avoids binary protobuf for initial human-editability
Verification combines static analysis (lint + permission checks) and dynamic rehearsal using a sandboxed namespace; trade-off: more complexity for higher operator safety
Idempotency contract: every oplet must declare a compensating action or a safe-guard flag; if absent verification fails
Telemetry gating will use a lightweight signalset (error-rate, p99 latency, request-throughput) to avoid overfitting to noisy metrics
Rollout will be PR-driven with optional scheduled promotions; avoids building a full UI workflow in MVP
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: rehearsal environment may miss real-world external dependencies -> Mitigation: record-and-replay harness and incident replay dataset to seed rehearsals
Risk: false sense of safety from lint-only checks -> Mitigation: require dynamic rehearsal pass for any oplet that touches infra state
Risk: delays in PR verification increasing CI time -> Mitigation: parallelize static checks and sandbox rehearsals, add CI timeout and allow expedites with oncall signoff
Risk: permission model complexity -> Mitigation: initial MVP restricts dangerous actions to 'approved' operators and requires escalation path
